changes.summary: Passkey management: `GET`, `PATCH` (rename) and `DELETE` on `/auth/webauthn/credentials` for the signed-in user's own passkeys. Passkeys now have a `name` (webauthn migration 0003): the one passed at registration, or the provider's name from its AAGUID (iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager, Windows Hello, 1Password…). `hasOtherSignInMethod` can protect the last passkey. The client gains `passkeys.rename`, a working `passkeys.list`, `runPasskeyRegistration(client, { name })` and `runPasskeyAuthentication` for a sign-in button.

Sessions record how and where they signed in: `signInMethod` (provider name, `passkey`, `password`, `magic_link`, `otp`, `sso`) and the User-Agent (sessions migration 0003). `GET /auth/sessions` returns them with a coarse `device` (`{ browser, os }`) via `describeUserAgent`; pass the callback's new `request` to `instantiateUserSession` to record OAuth sign-ins. The client's `sessions.list` now returns the array the server sends.

Sign-in identities: several provider accounts can open one user. New `identities` config mounts `GET /auth/identities` and `DELETE /auth/identities/:id` (never removes the last way in unless `hasOtherSignInMethod` says so); `linkCallbackIdentity` links the OAuth callback's account to the signed-in user from `onLinkIdentity` and throws `AuthIdentityConflictError` when another user already owns it, so `onLinkIdentityConflict` finally runs. Postgres/Neon and in-memory stores; migration block `identities` creates `auth_identities` (compatible with existing app tables and the CLI importer) with a unique provider+subject index.

Invitations accept an optional invitee name and personal note: stored with the invitation (organizations migration 0002), passed to onSendInvitation, and the name is returned when listing invitations. Name is trimmed to 200 characters; the note keeps line breaks and is limited to 2,000.

Add per-grant refresh-token family inventory and revocation: optional `listFamilies`, `getFamily` and `revokeFamily` store methods (in-memory and Postgres/Neon, with a family index migration), and pass the family id to `getAccessTokenClaims` so resource servers can reject access tokens from a revoked device immediately.
Bind WebAuthn ceremonies to single-use server records, purpose, user and session; add a durable Postgres challenge store and prevent credential owner/key replacement or counter rollback.

Add encrypted interactive-transaction OAuth credential coordination; serialize refresh and removal with grant row locks, persist recovery before returning failures, and reject stale or forged credential handles. Bound ambiguous token renewals and require reconnection after permanent failures.
Declare session and linking cookies on the OAuth authorization route so opt-in session binding accepts existing signed-in users. Add an authorization-start regression test.
Add owner-bound encrypted linked-provider grant storage, session-bound OAuth linking, and an exported OAuth authorization resolver for separately consented connectors.
Allow authorized nonmember organization managers to list memberships. Revoke invitations when their delivery hook fails and return a sanitized retryable error.

migration.instruction: Configure organizations.getVerifiedEmail with provider-verified email evidence. Direct acceptInvitation callers must supply verifiedEmail. Custom OrganizationStore adapters must implement atomic acceptInvitation; older adapters fail closed.

changes.summary: Bind organization invitation acceptance to a verified email and atomically consume the invitation with membership creation. Deny expired, revoked, missing-organization and suspended-member invitations; preserve existing member roles.
Include Neon in the typed built-in provider registry and configuration resolution

migration.instruction: Move createNeonProviderConfiguration results from customProviders.neon to providersConfiguration.neon. Neon is now a built-in Citra provider; credentials, scopes and offlineAccess inputs are unchanged.

migration.instruction: Send client_credentials requests to /auth/api/token instead of /oauth2/token and update advertised enterprise token URLs. Keep authorization_code and refresh_token requests at /oauth2/token. Prefer auth({ oidc, apikeys }) for configuration validation. API-only consumers may explicitly keep tokenRoute: /oauth2/token if no OIDC handler uses that path.
